title: Talking to a UC Santa Barbara class that had never heard of Tatum
summary: Callender asked students about Parker and Tatum and sent them Tatum albums from Norman Granz.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Oh, incidentally, I was at a Black History in the University of California, Santa Barbara, about a month ago. Professor Douglas Daniels, who is a young Black History professor up there, invited me to talk to the class. It's summer school, and I guess there were between 18 and 20 people in the class, and I think out of 18 to 20 there were 6 or 7 Black students. And I asked if anybody had ever heard of Charlie Parker, and nobody had ever heard of Charlie Parker except for one kid who was in high school -- he happened to be sitting in the class. And none of them had heard of Art Tatum. I thought this was pathetic. So I
asked everybody who had not heard of Art Tatum to come and write his name on a notebook I had. So I sent them all Art Tatum albums, thanks to Norman Granz.

Yeah. And I got a couple of letters from them, and they said it was marvelous. But strange thing, one letter said that he thought Art Tatum was great but he'd rather hear Benny Carter. I sent him the Benny Carter. Which was nice, you know, but the fact that these people could have lived in this century and not heard of Art Tatum was rather devastating.
Somebody ought to be teaching, or exposing them. Thank you for doing it.
